To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the virtual design of new lactones and isatins as hybrid chalcones (HLCICs) of falcipain (PfFP)-2 inhibitors, based on QSAR and pharmacophore models, has resulted in a new generation of potential anti-malarial agents with IC50pre values 100 times lower than that of the most active HLCIC1 inhibitor.
the QSAR model and 3D pharmacological model derived from it, are able to identify new HLCICs with superior inhibitory activity against FP-2.
the QSAR and the PH4 model are able to predict the potency of HLCIC inhibitors of the fP-2 cysteine proteases and to guide their design.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of novel HLCICs with high potential to become potent inhibitors of the fP2 cysteine proteases.
a virtual design of novel potent HLCICs for the treatment of malaria.
a virtual design of a novel class of HLCICs as potent and selective PfFP-2 inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our results are encouraging to continue the design of novel HLCICs and other inhibitors to target the PfFP-2 cysteine proteases.
our virtual approach is an excellent starting point for the design of new HLCICs.

the QSAR approach, in combination with the pharmacophore model and the intuitive substitution approach, has been a very powerful tool to design new HLCICs with superior activity to HLCIC1, which could be considered as potential new antimalarial drugs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PH4 is a reliable tool to design new HLCIC with improved activity against PfFP-2.
we have designed a series of 114 HLCICs with predicted IC50pre values in a range of 10–1000 nM, which are superior to that of our best training set inhibitor HLAIC1, which was 10 nM.
the PH4-based virtual screening of the focused library and intuitive substitution approach led to the discovery of 33 novel HLCICs with superior predicted potency and ADME profiles.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the QSAR approach can be used to predict the activity of new HLCIC compounds with a good accuracy and that it is a valuable tool to guide the design of new inhibitors of FP-2.
the QSAR model and PH4 can be used to virtually design new HLCICs that can be synthesized and tested against PfFP-2.
virtual screening can be used as a powerful tool for the discovery of novel and potentially potent inhibitors of P. falciparum proteases.
